Model & sources

From local conditions to kelp biomass

Temperature, light, nitrate and currents→Growth and internal nitrogen→Biomass, respiration and tissue loss

Saccharina longissima

The mature-thallus model follows 99 stations in eastern Hokkaido. Historical runs cover 1996–2020; two single-forcing scenarios cover 2021–2100. The first five future years are an adjustment period. Optical attenuation was fitted to Habomai observations from 2001–2006; the 2007–2014 comparison is retrospective temporal evaluation.

Habomai evaluation · 2007–2014

MonthAnnual-median rAnnual-median RMSE (g DW)
May0.89120.63

Eight annual medians in each month; the comparison assesses shared temporal variation, not independent validation of every station.

Parameters and interpretation

The adopted run uses I₀ = 180 W m⁻², effective depth 1.7 m and fitted TPM = 20.43 mg L⁻¹. Temperature, light and internal nitrogen multiply to constrain potential growth. Respiratory loss increases with temperature. Detachment responds to current speed and individual mass.

Stations are independent, with no horizontal transport. Fixed optics and unresolved waves limit local interpretation. Detached material is a source for transport studies; it is not measured carbon sequestration. The portal shows per-thallus outputs, without applying bed-area or density multipliers.

Saccharina japonica

The completed 1,930-station scenario covers 1991–2020. It carries individual mass, internal nitrogen, mature density and tissue condition continuously through the record. One planned station was excluded because its current mapping exceeded the accepted distance.

Scenario assumptions

Bed biomass is mass per individual multiplied by modeled mature density, per occupied bed area. Density, mature entry and thermal tissue wear are scenario assumptions; they are not regional field measurements. Mature-entry tissue is an external input to the modeled mature compartment.

Physical conditions use FORA–JPN60. Nitrate uses JRA55-do through 2018, then stored GFDL-ESM2M RCP2.6 in 2019–2020. The source change is marked in the charts. This historical sensitivity scenario is not a dated local reconstruction or a future projection. No completed future Japonica run is provided.

Display records and downloads

Monthly curves are calendar-month means of native daily model outputs. Annual states and factors are means; annual fluxes are sums. Individual annual peaks use native internal-step maxima for Longissima and native daily states for Japonica. Point records are rounded for display; CSV files include the rounding bounds. Raw environmental forcing and private manuscript files are not distributed.
